_README: Hand-maintained. Everything else in this directory is derived by scripts/wiring-map.mjs from the source. These are the few edges a walker cannot see: a human running a command, a file produced on another machine, a value a person has to type. Anything asserted here is marked ASSERTED wherever it appears in the output, so a reader can always tell what was proved from what was claimed. Keep this file small. If something here can be derived instead, derive it.

asserted_producers.nfl_availability_rates: Produced by `node scripts/fit-availability.mjs` over a shell on the machine. There is no route and no job that runs it, by design: it is a 5-season fit with a 2,000-draw bootstrap.
asserted_producers.nfl_availability_role_rates: Same script, and only if its pre-registered gate passes on held-out 2025. A failed gate writes zero rows on purpose; an empty table is a legitimate outcome, not a bug.
asserted_producers.espn_player_market: syncEspnMarket() exists and nothing calls it. Not a deliberate manual step — an unfinished one.
asserted_producers.league_roster_snapshots: `node scripts/collect-roster-snapshots.mjs`, run by hand per league.
asserted_producers.league_transactions_raw: `node scripts/collect-league-transactions.mjs`, run by hand per league.
asserted_producers.negotiation_profiles: Lives in the CHAT database, not the app's — built by scripts/build-negotiation-profiles.mjs on the Mac and delivered inside the corpus file.
asserted_producers.nfl_rebuild_progress: Written by the 2022-2025 rebuild script while it runs. Correctly manual.
asserted_producers.nfl_rebuild_checkpoints: Written by the 2022-2025 rebuild script while it runs. Correctly manual.
asserted_producers.manager_archetypes: Written by server/services/manager-archetypes.js:561-563, driven by scripts/build-manager-archetypes.mjs. No chat dependency — it replays league-seasons out of the app's own database, so it works whether or not a corpus ever arrives. PR #26 registers it as a scheduled job (scheduler.js, heavy tier, 24h).

notes.league_member_identity: The walker sees a writer (manager-identity.js) reachable from a route and calls the table fed. It is not, in the way that matters: a row only becomes usable to the Trade Brain when its `confidence` is 'confirmed' or 'exact' (TRUSTED_CONFIDENCE), and 'confirmed' is only ever set from the `confirmations` argument, which a person has to supply. Name matching cannot bootstrap it, because chat handles are not ESPN names. A value-level dependency like this one is outside what an import-and-SQL walker can prove, which is why it is written down here.
notes.espn_settings: Read once at server/db/index.js:228 to migrate a pre-multi-league row into `leagues`. Nothing writes it any more and nothing should. Kept as a legacy read.
notes.scope: Betting rows are mapped and tagged `betting`. They are out of scope for work and in scope for knowing — a map with a hole in it is worse than no map, because people trust it.
notes.the chat corpus: messages, jev_chat_signals, manager_chat_profile, manager_player_sentiment and negotiation_profiles are NOT in the app's database. They are Nick's iMessage corpus, a separate SQLite file opened read-only via chatDbPath()/messagesDbPath(), built on his Mac and delivered whole through POST /api/league-chat/upload (which refuses a corpus with an empty messages table). The map reported all four as 'written by nothing' before it learned to tell the two handles apart; they were fine. Both consuming surfaces already refuse and name the gap when the corpus is absent.

_ACCEPTED_README: accepted_missing_feeds is a RATCHET, not approval. Each entry is a gap that already existed when the check was turned on, so CI fails on anything NEW rather than on day one. Fixing one means deleting its line here. Nothing should ever be added to this list to make a build pass — add it only when turning the check on over existing debt. Entries with a rule name in front come from the should-wire family: a column nothing writes, or a producer nothing calls. They are real and they are pre-existing; the gate exists so the eleventh does not become the twelfth silently.
_ORPHAN_README: Modules that exist today and reach no live surface. Every one was checked on 2026-09-19: they are deliberate research, a measured-and-declined experiment, or half of a split that never finished. They are listed so the build fails on the NEXT one, not on these. Adding to this list is how you say out loud that a module is landing unwired on purpose - put the reason in the review, not here.

Each carries the condition that would RETIRE it, so the list cannot rot into a junk drawer. If the condition is met and the module is still listed, that is a defect in this file, not in the module.
_PERMANENT_ORPHAN_REASONS.server/services/opportunity-model.js: O1 research model (PR #15). Deliberately unwired: measured against its own baselines in scripts/study-opportunity-volume.mjs and the effect is inside the noise on every head - RB carries -0.86% and -0.98% across two seasons, pooled 90% intervals [-0.077,+0.027] and [-0.092,+0.037], both straddling zero; the full sixteen-feature ridge is WORSE than an exponentially-weighted average of the player's own recent volume by +7.5% and +10.7%. The mechanism is real (a vacated same-position share carries a positive coefficient, 0.49 to 1.65 in log space, in every position and season); the payoff is not. Fourth attempt at this question in this repository, agreeing with the previous three. Promotion needs a season it has not been fitted on. RETIRE THIS ENTRY WHEN: a season the model has not seen, graded the same way, puts RB carries clear of zero on the pooled interval - 2026 once it finishes, not before. Wiring it earlier should fail this check rather than edit this line. See docs/OPPORTUNITY-FINDINGS-2026-09-19.md section 3. Owner: the Opportunity thread. NOTE: what actually shipped from O1 is the volume shrinkage constants, which land as a database write rather than a caller - projections.js shrinks share with K.share=6 and team volume with K.team_volume=10 against fitted values of 0.08-0.28 and 1.3-1.7. That is the real defect from this work and this map cannot see it, because a constant that should be a fitted row has no edge.
_PERMANENT_ORPHAN_REASONS.server/services/cascade-grade.js: PRE-REGISTERED: the file is not in this tree yet, it arrives with PR #72, and the --check run reports it as an accept-list entry naming a missing file until it does. Held-out grader for contingency.js#cascades (PR #72). Deliberately unwired and reached only by scripts/grade-cascade-multipliers.mjs, the same shape as opportunity-model.js behind study-opportunity-volume.mjs: it exists to grade a shipped estimator walk-forward, not to serve anything. It lives in a service rather than inside the script so the row construction is unit-testable: test/cascade-grade.test.js pins absence-without-a-box-score-row, the span bound and the strictly-prior baseline. RETIRE THIS ENTRY WHEN the grade is promoted to something a surface reads, which it is not today; the grade REFUSED the published multipliers in both seasons. Owner: the Opportunity thread.
_PERMANENT_ORPHAN_REASONS.server/services/vegas-fantasy.js: Orphaned on 2026-09-20 by this branch, not by neglect: its only importers were GET /api/model/game-script, /game-script/:team and /game-script-fit, three routes nothing called, deleted in the same commit. The module itself is real, measured work — a market-implied-total layer for fantasy projections, r = 0.41 over 2,106 team-weeks since 2022, monotone across every bucket, with the components scaled separately because they scale differently. IT IS NOT DELETED, DELIBERATELY. Deleting it would throw away a fitted model to close a report, and whether a measured model ships is Nick's call, not a wiring cleanup's. THE HAZARD TO READ BEFORE TOUCHING IT: server/services/gamescript.js exports fitGameScript, gameScriptFor and clearGameScriptCache TOO, and gameScriptFor takes its arguments in a DIFFERENT ORDER — (team, season, week) there against (season, week, team, opts) here. routes/model.js imported from both files at once. Anyone wiring this up by autocompleting the name gets silently wrong answers with no error, which is the two-names-different-sources failure in its worst form: one name, two sources, incompatible signatures. RETIRE THIS ENTRY WHEN either a surface reads it (and the name collision with gamescript.js is resolved first) or Nick says the layer is not wanted, at which point the file is deleted rather than listed.

_NEVER_BASELINE._why: producer-with-no-caller CANNOT be silenced from this file. The list of protected rules, and the six grandfathered exceptions, live in NEVER_BASELINE and GRANDFATHERED in scripts/wiring-map.mjs - deliberately in the checker's own source and not here, because a never-baseline list that the check reads out of the file it is policing can be removed by the same edit it exists to prevent. Silencing one is a code review with a name on it, not a data edit. An entry added here naming that rule is refused, reported by name on every run, and has no effect. Raised by the Opportunity thread, 2026-09-19.
